recent_posts.title: Prepare your app for Accessibility Nutrition Labels | Apple Developer
recent_posts.summary: Apple's accessibility team walks through how to prepare iOS/macOS apps for App Store's new 'accessibility nutrition labels', which let users know which accessibility features an app supports before downloading. The guide covers VoiceOver support (labels, traits, values, grouping, custom gestures), Dynamic Type for larger text sizes (system font styles, layout changes, ScrollView usage, SwiftUI previews), and color accessibility (differentiate without color, Dark Mode, contrast settings, and the new 'liquid glass' design system). Code examples use both SwiftUI and UIKit APIs throughout.

recent_posts.title: Accelerate your machine learning workloads with the M5 and A19 GPUs | Apple Developer
recent_posts.summary: Apple's M5 and A19 GPUs introduce neural accelerators — dedicated matrix multiplication hardware built into every shader core — delivering up to 4x faster LLM time-to-first-token and 7.7x faster AI video enhancement with no code changes. The talk covers the architecture of neural accelerators, the Metal TensorOps API (including new bfloat16, cooperative tensor, and 4/8-bit integer support in iOS/macOS 26), and how to build tiled matrix multiplication kernels with activation fusion. Key optimization techniques include tuning tile sizes, SIMD group synchronization with threadgroup barriers, and Morton-order threadgroup traversal for better cache locality. Profiling workflows using Metal System Trace and the Xcode Metal Debugger are demonstrated, showing a nearly 7x speedup on a 4K×4K matmul by adopting TensorOps and Morton-order dispatch.

recent_posts.title: Boost your graphics performance with the M5 and A19 GPUs | Apple Developer
recent_posts.summary: Apple's M5 and A19 GPU family introduces the 'Family 10' GPU architecture with significant performance improvements. Key automatic gains include 2x faster FP16/complex ALU execution, doubled geometry throughput, 30% more memory bandwidth, second-generation dynamic caching with a smarter occupancy management unit, universal texture compression (now covering compute shaders), and third-generation hardware ray tracing with 70% faster intersection function buffer indexing and reduced memory alignment from 16KB to 1KB. New opt-in features include extended indirect command buffers (ICBs) allowing full GPU-driven pipelines with per-draw device state encoding, visibility buffer rendering, depth bound testing, 8x MSAA resolved on-chip, and 32K texture support. Xcode 26.4 adds new occupancy profiling counters (register pressure, L1 cache pressure, memory stalls, texture decompression stalls) to diagnose and fix low GPU occupancy. Best practices for universal texture compression are covered, including when to disable it for scattered access patterns using the compression ratio and write inefficiency counters.

recent_posts.title: Meet agentic coding in Xcode | Apple Developer
recent_posts.summary: Xcode 26.3 introduces agentic coding powered by the Model Context Protocol, enabling AI agents like Claude and OpenAI Codex to autonomously handle complex, multi-step development tasks. The feature allows agents to analyze project structure, search documentation, generate code, add entitlements, fix build errors, and iterate automatically. A demo shows an agent adding WeatherKit integration and a seven-day forecast view with Liquid Glass to a sample app, creating over 400 lines of code across three files in minutes. The MCP-based approach supports any compatible agent, with one-click downloads and automatic updates for Anthropic and OpenAI tools.

recent_posts.title: Apple announces 2026 Swift Student Challenge with design guidance
recent_posts.summary: Apple announces the 2026 Swift Student Challenge, a free worldwide competition for student developers running February 6-28. Students can submit apps built with Xcode or Swift Playgrounds on any topic. The session covers app design principles including Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and the new Liquid Glass material, walks through the four-phase design process (discover, prototype, validate, iterate), and features interviews with previous winners who built EyeSee (simulating vision conditions) and EvacuMate (wildfire evacuation assistant). Emphasis is placed on solving meaningful problems, iterative design, accessibility, and using standard components rather than building overly complex features.

recent_posts.title: Apple announces Swift Student Challenge 2026
recent_posts.summary: Apple announces the Swift Student Challenge 2026, inviting students to participate in an online event featuring Apple experts and past winners. Participants can learn and find inspiration for creating app playground submissions for the competition.

recent_posts.title: Discover the Apple Design Resources
recent_posts.summary: Apple provides design resources including UI kits for Figma and Sketch, hardware bezels, and tools like SF Symbols to help designers create accurate app mockups. These resources are available through developer.apple.com/design/resources, Figma's asset panel, and Sketch's library settings. The kits include pre-built components with examples, support for dark mode visualization, and automatic updates when Apple changes system components. Using these resources alongside the Human Interface Guidelines ensures designs accurately represent how apps will look on Apple platforms.

recent_posts.title: Liquid Glass Showcase: Tide Guide | Meet with Apple
recent_posts.summary: Tide Guide's founder demonstrates implementing Apple's Liquid Glass design system across iOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and macOS. The presentation covers interactive button effects, glass materials, identity variants for subtle animations, custom popovers for settings, and system-wide improvements like concentricity and consistent alignment. Key insights include how small visual refinements dramatically improve interface feel, the flexibility of glass effects beyond standard components, and that adopting the new design doesn't require a full redesign—many improvements come from simply using latest system components.

recent_posts.title: Liquid Glass Showcase: CNN | Meet with Apple
recent_posts.summary: CNN's Director of Apps shares their experience adopting SwiftUI and Apple's Liquid Glass design system for their iOS app. The team migrated from a mixed Objective-C/UIKit/React Native codebase to SwiftUI, which simplified article rendering and improved development velocity. Liquid Glass integration brought challenges including nested glass effect modifiers, padding behavior issues, and performance considerations in scrollable views. The team created custom view modifiers for conditional application and established guidelines to prevent visual redundancy. They plan to extend the shared codebase to tvOS and are creating a dedicated squad for platform-specific innovation.

recent_posts.title: Liquid Glass Showcase: Slack | Meet with Apple
recent_posts.summary: Slack's product team shares their approach to redesigning their iOS app for iOS 26's Liquid Glass design language. The redesign was driven by Slack's product philosophy of making work simpler and more pleasant, while simultaneously improving core functionality like search accessibility. The team prototyped multiple header designs, moved search to the tab bar for global availability, and adopted native controls to future-proof the app. They rolled out changes incrementally—prioritizing high-traffic areas first in September, releasing riskier changes in October, and continuing polish through November and December. Using native OS controls allowed the team to focus on Slack-specific features while the platform handled standard UI patterns.

top_posts.title: WWDC21: Discoverable design | Apple
top_posts.summary: Jiabao Li and Mylène Dreyer from Apple's Prototyping team discuss methods for making app interfaces more discoverable. They introduce principles like prioritizing important features, using familiar words and symbols as visual cues, incorporating standard gestures, organizing content by user behavior, and conveying a sense of control through feedback mechanisms. These techniques aim to ensure users can easily navigate and fully utilize app features without needing extensive onboarding tutorials.

top_posts.title: WWDC23: Create immersive Unity apps | Apple
top_posts.summary: Unity has collaborated with Apple to bring Unity support for immersive apps on a new platform. There are two main approaches for creating immersive experiences: mixing content with real-world objects using passthrough or bringing a fully immersive Unity experience. Unity provides tools and capabilities for achieving desired visual look, entering play mode directly to device, and controlling how content is brought into the real world. Unity PolySpatial helps translate materials and rendering between Unity and RealityKit. Different types of volumes and input types are available for interaction. Developers can start preparing their projects today for spatial computing on Apple platforms.

top_posts.title: WWDC24: Work with windows in SwiftUI | Apple
top_posts.summary: Learn how to work with windows in SwiftUI, including defining, opening, and using windows, controlling initial window placement, and sizing windows. Enhance windows with platform-specific features in visionOS.

top_posts.title: WWDC23: Meet watchOS 10 | Apple
top_posts.summary: watchOS 10 introduces significant changes to Apple Watch, including new features, a redesigned user interface, and recommended design principles for app development.

top_posts.title: WWDC21: What‘s new in Swift | Apple
top_posts.summary: Swift 5.5 introduces major updates, including Swift Concurrency for efficient and safe asynchronous programming, as well as improvements to the package experience and developer productivity. The community gets a boost with the Diversity in Swift initiative and mentorship programs. New features like DocC for documentation, enhancements in type checking, and tools like Swift Collections, Swift Algorithms, and Swift Numerics refine the developer experience. Swift's new async/await syntax simplifies concurrent code, while actors ensure thread safety.
